newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar creeps higher, trade supportive.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar creeps higher, trade supportive.

text.p: White sugar futures nudged higher in London's last session before the extended holiday break as buying from one leading trade house supported nearby values, market sources said on Tuesday.

At the early close, the market re-opens December 27, most of the turnover derived from crossed trades on the spot March contract and some light activity was also seen on the March/May and other spreads.
"The spread has gone out a bit...but it's been a pretty mixed bag and apart from a couple of spreads there's really nothing going on," said one trader.

March was down 10 cents at $306.40 and May up 10 cents at $306.40. Volume amounted to a scant 315 lots. Technical analysts pegged resistance at $308.00 basis March but said there was enough momentum for the level to be broken after the position moved above $305.00 during Monday's session. In physical news, Pakistan's TCP bought 50,000 tonnes of sugar at $350 and $360 per tonne for delivery by January 11.

The State Trading Corporation of India is to deliver 25,000 tonnes at $350 per tonne FOB basis via Wagah border and the Indian Sugar and General Industry Corp 25,000 tonnes at $360 per tonne CFFO basis by sea to Karachi port.
Jordanian traders said Iraq bought two sugar cargoes this week of between 14,000 and 15,000 tonnes each, one Brazilian and the other European origin.

Most of the 120 offers by international sugar houses -- said to number around 120 -- which Iraq was evaluating were between $370 per tonne for Brazilian origin and $380 per tonne for European origin sugar, they said.
But Iraq's counter-offers of $366 per tonne to at least 10 suppliers were rejected by the suppliers as too low.
